H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper gives separate flat entry/exit flowcharts and physical floors, but no nested controller modes or composite state structure.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Entry depends on RFID validity plus occupancy availability; full capacity is derived from six IR space sensors, and exit depends on whether the card was checked in.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Actions include opening/not opening gates, LCD Access Allowed/Denied/FULL displays, LED occupancy indicators, database updates, and counter increment/decrement.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: No emergency stop, fault rollback, fail-safe transition, or recovery path is described.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: RFID authorization is introduced in the abstract/design section, full-capacity blocking in the sensor section, LCD/LED responses in test-running, and counter/database updates in the entry/exit sequence section.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as RFID validation and checked-in status are accompanied by explicit yes/no flowchart behavior, so no external domain rule is required.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: LCD and LED actions are described in prose/test results rather than co-located with the entry/exit flowchart actions.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The effective entry guard combines valid RFID card with capacity availability, and FULL depends on all parking-space sensors being engaged.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No parent/composite state with entry/during/exit behavior is present.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: No from-any-state fault or recovery rule is declared.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No composite-state initialization or pseudo-state routing is needed.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: There are one to two meaningful composed guards around RFID validity, checked-in status, and occupancy/fullness.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: The sample does not define a global forced transition or a parent-mode during monitor that would clearly save N explicit transitions.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Database update and availability indication are abstract side effects, although most outputs are concrete LCD, LED, and servo commands.

key_nl_quotes: When all spaces are engaged, the Arduino will not enable the servo motor to open the entrance gate anymore and FULL will be displayed.
When the driver places a valid RFID card on the reader, the entrance gate opens, the car enters the park and the counter increases by one.
one_line_pitch: This is a compact but useful guard/action stress test because authorization, occupancy, display, gate actuation, and database/counter updates are distributed across the paper rather than specified in one formal block.
rationale: The sample is meaningful because it stresses the two weakest baseline areas: guarded decisions and transition actions. Its strongest complexity comes from RFID-plus-occupancy guards and multiple side effects, including servo commands, LCD/LED outputs, database update, and counter changes. It lacks hierarchical modes and fault recovery, so it is better as a backup stress-test case than a top candidate.
